title: Fast top-1000 TCP scan
description: Service/version detection plus default scripts. -oA saves grepable, normal and XML output at once.
output: Open ports with service, version and any script hits (e.g. 22/tcp open ssh OpenSSH 8.9).

title: Full TCP port sweep
description: All 65535 ports quickly, then re-scan the open ones with -sV -sC for detail.
output: Complete list of open TCP ports. Feed these into a targeted second scan.

title: UDP top ports
description: UDP is slow; scan only common ports. Watch for SNMP (161), DNS (53), IKE (500).
output: open|filtered results. Confirm interesting ones with a service-specific tool.

title: Rapid port discovery into nmap
description: Very fast port discovery, then pipes into nmap for detail. Good when nmap -p- feels slow.
output: Same nmap detail output, reached far faster on responsive hosts.

title: WAF-safe decoy SYN scan
description: -D RND:20 sprays 20 random decoy source IPs to hide the real scanner from WAFs/blacklists. -sS SYN scan, --open shows only open ports.
output: Open ports only, with your real source address blended among 20 decoys.

title: Fast all-ports SYN scan
description: No WAF/rate-limiting in the way? Blast all 65535 ports at 60k packets/s, then re-scan the open ones with -sV.
output: Every open TCP port, fast. Feed these into a targeted -sV scan.

title: Targeted service/version scan
description: After finding open ports, probe just those to pin down the exact service and version running.
output: Service + version per port to match against known exploits.

title: NSE vulnerability script
description: Run an NSE script from /usr/share/nmap/scripts against a service; grep script.db to find scripts. Pass arguments with --script-args cmd=id.
output: Script output, e.g. confirmation the vsftpd backdoor is exploitable.

title: Search-engine dorking for files
description: Terminal browser that dumps a page as text, ideal for scraping search-engine results (site: + ext: dorks) to harvest exposed documents. Loop wget over the list, then read metadata with exiftool.
output: A list of document URLs from the results, ready to download and inspect.

title: Dump a web page as text
description: Render a page to plain text in the terminal, quick content review and link harvesting without a browser.
output: The page's visible text and links printed to stdout.
